claims.claim: bottom invertebrates made up about 50 % of the prey of 470 fish populations
claims.location: p. 2152 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; p. 2155 (PDF p. 4), Results and Table 1 (means row)
claims.quote: Across all species considered, zoobenthos averaged 50% of total prey consumption.
claims.conditions: diet data (percentage of gut volume or mass) for adults of 13 species, 470 populations (146,895 fish) in north-temperate North American lakes; the mean is the mean of species means (Table 1: zooplankton 20 %, zoobenthos 48 %, fish 32 %); 'zoobenthos' includes littoral and profundal invertebrates, aquatic insects and detritus (< 1.5 %)
claims.note: the Results give 48 % (Table 1), the abstract rounds to 50 %. It is a species average, not a population-weighted one: species ranged from 99 % (pumpkinseed) to 14–15 % (walleye, cisco). The paper's '(abstract only)' can now be dropped.

claims.claim: or about 65 % counting the bottom-feeding fish that piscivores eat
claims.location: p. 2152 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; p. 2155 (PDF p. 4), Results
claims.quote: for a total of 65% reliance on benthic secondary production
claims.conditions: direct zoobenthivory plus 'indirect' (prey fish supported by zoobenthos, eq. 1); a conservative 50 % benthivory was assumed for the fish eaten by smallmouth, rock and largemouth bass, whose prey fish were not resolved
claims.note: the Results give 64 % (Table 1: direct and indirect); the abstract says 65 %. Stable isotopes gave 43–59 % littoral reliance (90 populations, 11 species, 18 Ontario and Quebec lakes).

notes: The paper's two numbers are right and correctly described; only the code comments blur direct and indirect benthic support. The source does not say the benthic share is higher in small lakes (the §3.7.9 lead-in 'In small lakes much of this production rests on the bottom'), but it does report that lake trout in lakes > 10 km² ate no zoobenthos while those in lakes < 10 km² often ate much (Fig. 2, p. 2157) and that lake size and basin morphometry set the littoral's importance (Discussion, p. 2158) — usable support for the small-lake framing if cited that way. Species values of interest for Hot Brook (Table 1, direct zoobenthos % of diet): pumpkinseed 99, yellow perch 68, rock bass 86, smallmouth bass 57, largemouth 36, northern pike 14; isotope littoral reliance (Table 2, 0‰ fractionation): pumpkinseed 98, yellow perch 72, smallmouth 100, pike 74 (one population). The abstract says '470 fish populations (15 species)' while Table 1 lists 13 species rows (its 'whitefishes' row includes Prosopium and its 'sculpins' row is Cottus sp.); say '13 species groups' or quote the abstract's 15. Table 1 values above were read on the page image.
